items.title: Email Campaign · : Concierge "Is it worth it?" Campaign
items.preview:
**Why this one:** 100 candidates already past their year-1 service (trust is established, no Rule 1 violation). This is the highest-intent, warmest paid-conversion play available this week. $99/mo recurring revenue with a defensible "here's the math" angle.
**1. Campaign name + audience size**
Concierge Year-1.5 Math Check. **100 recipients** (13-24mo post-install, not on Concierge)
**2. Subject line (60 char max) + alternates**
- Primary: `The question we get at 18 months` (32)
- Alt A (curiosity): `Is Concierge actually worth it for you?` (40)
- Alt B (pain): `Who handles your filter swaps right now?` (41)
- Alt C (authority): `The math on year-two water care` (32)
- Alt D (specific): `$99/mo, or the pay-as-you-go route?` (35)
**3. Preview text (90 char max)**
`No pressure. Just the honest breakdown so you can decide what fits your home.` (76)
**4. Email body**
Hi [First Name],
You are past your first year with your [System], which means the honest question tends to show up around now: is the Concierge plan worth it for me, or should I keep going pay-as-you-go?
Fair question. Here is the math, no spin.
Concierge is $99/mo. It covers your annual service, filter swaps, priority phone support, and parts coverage on the standard install components. If you would rather book each visit and each filter separately, that works too. A lot of our clients do.
The people who tend to like Concierge: those who would rather not track service dates, and who want a real person on the phone fast when something comes up.
If you want, reply "math" and I will lay out the year-two numbers for your specific setup. If pay-as-you-go suits you better, no follow-up, I promise.
Justin
CEO / ClearWave
**5. Send timing**
Tuesday, 10:00 AM ET (mid-morning, top of week, past Monday inbox flood; matches your 42% baseline open window).
**6. Expected performance**
- Open: **40-45%** (matches your list baseline; warm, named, non-promotional subject)
- Click/reply: **3-6%** (reply-driven, not link-driven. Your click metric is near-zero because past campaigns pushed app links nobody wanted; a reply CTA sidesteps that entirely)
- Conversion: **4-8 sign-ups** at $99/mo = **$396-$792/mo recurring** ($4.7K-$9.5K/yr). High-margin.
**7. Source justification**
Draws from **CONCIERGE UPSELL CONTEXT** (the "year 1.5 is it worth it / here's the math" framing verbatim) and **JOBBER LIFECYCLE TRIGGERS → Concierge upsell candidates** (pre-filtered to 13-24mo, satisfying Rule 1's 12-month floor).

items.title: Email Campaign · : Referral Push (30-60 Day Post-Install)
items.preview:
**Why this one:** 30 recently-installed, satisfied clients at peak "new water is noticeably better" enthusiasm. Referrals are our approved growth lever (Rule 3), and the $500 first-referral hook is concrete.
**1. Campaign name + audience size**
Fresh-Install Referral Push. **30 recipients** (30-60 days post-install, satisfied)
**2. Subject line (60 char max) + alternates**
- Primary: `Know someone drinking bad water?` (32)
- Alt A (specific): `$500 when your referral becomes a client` (41)
- Alt B (curiosity): `A quick favor (there's $500 in it)` (34)
- Alt C (authority): `Your water is dialed in. Their turn?` (36)
- Alt D (pain): `Tired of hearing your friends complain?` (40)
**3. Preview text (90 char max)**
`$500 per closed referral. A gift card even if they just book. Here is how it works.` (82)
**4. Email body**
Hi [First Name],
You are about a month into life with your [System], which is right around when most people stop thinking about their water at all. That is the goal.
Quick ask. If a friend, neighbor, or family member is dealing with water they do not trust, send them our way.
Here is how the referral works:
- If they become a client: **$500 cash** for your first through fifth referral this year, $750 for six through nine, $1,000 at ten or more.
- If they just book a consult and do not move forward: **$50 gift card**, on us.
All they need is a free water assessment to get started. Reply with their name and the best way to reach them, or forward them this email.
Thanks for trusting us with your home.
Justin
CEO / ClearWave
**5. Send timing**
Thursday, 11:00 AM ET (late-week, avoids overlap with Tuesday's Concierge send to a different segment).
**6. Expected performance**
- Open: **42-48%** (small warm list, recent positive experience, personal tone)
- Reply/forward: **5-10%** (reply-and-forward CTA, no dead app link)
- Conversion: **1-3 booked consults** near-term; even one closed referral pays for itself many times over. Referral leads close at higher rates than cold, so downstream value is strong.
**7. Source justification**
Draws from **REFERRAL BONUS STRUCTURE** (exact $500/$750/$1,000 and $50 gift card tiers), **Rule 3** (referrals over reviews), **Rule 3a** ("free water assessment" exact phrasing), and **JOBBER LIFECYCLE TRIGGERS → Referral push candidates** (30-60 day satisfied segment).
---
### Notes on what I deliberately skipped
- **Cold lead re-engagement (1,000):** high volume but lowest intent, and it needs a fresh water-news angle I would want sourced/verified before sending to a stale segment (deliverability risk to 1,000 cold contacts could hurt your strong 42% sender reputation). Worth doing, but as a separate carefully-warmed send, not a rushed same-week play.
- **1-year annual service (19):** operational reminder, not a conversion campaign, and too small to headline. Note Eric Berg appears twice (one $0 duplicate). Dedupe before any send.
Both proposals above use real product names in the `[System]` merge field per Rule 2, avoid all em/en dashes per Rule 5, and never pitch Concierge before the 12-month floor per Rule 1.
